messages.author: 09ad8d237e8d8786
messages.subject: repeated measure GAMM
parts:
Dear group,

I was trying to implement a GAMM using the z model facility, and ran into a crash while fitting a repeated measure model, the model looks like
gamm(freq~s(SST)+s(WE,bs='cp')+s(CHLA)+(1|transmitter), correlation=corAR1(~time|transmitter)
in the nlme syntax. I used f(time,model="ar1", replicate=transmitter) to implement the AR1 correlation structure.
There were 325 transmitters and 107 time periods, so the time random effect should have length about 37000. When the code was run on a Linux cluster, the time random effect was of length 6 million, way over the expected length. And INLA crashed after a while. 

Attached please find the rda and code that should replicate the huge random effect and crash. The Linux cluster is running Ubuntu 18.04, and INLA build is 2019-09-03 (the recent stable version) . Can you please look into this?

Thanks
dong

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] repeated measure GAMM
parts:
the issue is this

> range(dat$transmitter)
[1] 11052 57019
> length(unique(dat$transmitter2))
[1] 342


the 'replicate' argument assume values 1,2,3,...,K, and it will
replicate K times. with the above, it will replicate 57019 times, but
since there are only 342 unique values, it will only need to replicate
342 times.

so I added

dat$transmitter = as.numeric(as.factor(dat$transmitter))
dat$transmitter2 = as.numeric(as.factor(dat$transmitter2))

to do this, but you probably want to do this more carefully.

H
